youtube.title: Why Train Tracks Have Stones Under Them 🚆 #Shorts #science #facts #didyouknow
youtube.description:
Those stones under railway tracks are called ballast, and they're crushed with sharp edges on purpose so they lock together instead of rolling. Every passing train pushes down on the sleepers; the stones spread that weight, hold the sleepers in place and let monsoon rainwater drain straight through. Without them, heavy trains would slowly push the track out of line.
